hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: One probe. If the mixed-spelling form still emits a single load, MWCC's CSE is address-based rather than expression-based here and the whole two-load shape is unreachable from source, which would close this axis for good rather than leaving it open.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - derived by reading fnasm.py game/game/player do_players 0x230:0x290 --diff, which is where the identical-address/two-base-form fact was measured; NOT yet probed as a source edit.
hypothesis.statement: The aligned view at @0x24c (and its twin at @0x6c4) shows the target loading THE SAME ADDRESS TWICE through TWO DIFFERENT base forms: `lwz r0,232(r18)` with r18 = r31+3136 for the `!= 0` test, then `add r3,r31,r16` / `lwz r0,3368(r3)` for the `== 2 || == 3` test, where 3136+232 == 3368 == the same field of the same player. We emit ONE load and reuse it. Probe C proves the duplication is NOT reachable by re-reading the SAME expression (MWCC CSEs identical spellings straight back to one load, object bytes unchanged). The remaining untried idea is therefore to make the two reads TEXTUALLY DIFFERENT SPELLINGS of the same address - e.g. keep the walked-pointer/`p`-relative spelling for the `!= 0` test and use `PTA(j)->state` only for the 2/3 pair - so that MWCC's CSE cannot see through them, which is the one configuration that produces the target's two-load, two-base shape.
